verdict.reasoning: Transcript confirms age 27 ("I am 7. 27" / Doctor repeats "27"), but the patient's gender is never stated; calling the patient male is additional information.

Patient reports diarrhea for about three days ("it's been about three days now"), describes very watery stools ("just super watery"), occurring about every hour while awake ("almost every hour I'm awake"), and denies blood ("No, I don't remember anything...There's nothing like that").

Patient says the crampy pain is in the middle lower abdomen, not one side ("it's like at the bottom" and "it feels pretty like in the middle to me. Not on any side. Left or right"), and rates it about 6–7/10. The fact states left lower quadrant, which contradicts the localization.
Patient explicitly reports feeling nauseous ("Yeah, I definitely feel kind of nauseous").
Patient describes vomiting after milk ("whenever I have, like, milk...I want to vomit. And actually, yeah, one time I just, like, had some milk and I just completely vomited it").
Patient states they are avoiding milk ("I've been trying to avoid it" referring to milk).
Patient feels hot but has not measured their temperature ("I feel kind of really hot all the time" and "I haven't actually done any temperature reading").
Patient confirms passing urine but less frequently (Doctor: "Are you passing urine?" Patient: "Yeah, but I guess less frequently maybe, but it seems to be okay").
Patient reports brother has had similar symptoms for about five days ("my, my brother has had, actually had something like this for. He has it as well, for five days as well").
Patient reports being otherwise fit and well and no related history ("Yeah, I think otherwise I'm fit. Well...I can't think of any related medical history...no, I don't think so").
Patient denies regular medications (Doctor: "You don't take any regular medications then?" Patient: "No...I'm not on any regular medication or anything like that").
Patient reports taking paracetamol lately ("I've been taking some, like, paracetamols and stuff like that lately").

Doctor advises continued paracetamol use as needed ("You can try just, you know, regular paracetamol if you are feeling feverish" and later "Is it okay for me to carry on having like paracetamol..." Doctor: "Absolutely. If...bit of tummy pain, if you're feeling feverish, then I think paracetamol is very sensible").
Patient denies known allergies (Doctor: "do you have any allergies..." Patient: "I don't have any allergies that I know of").
Patient states father has colon cancer and describes it as third stage ("My dad actually has colon cancer at the moment" and "he's sort of in his third stage"). Stage III matches third stage.
Patient says they live with sister and mother ("I live with my um, sister and my mum").
Patient works in a government office ("I work at an office in central London. It's. So I work in government").
Patient describes smoking socially ("I smoke, I smoke for like socially but not like regularly. So normally if it's a Friday...I might have a cigarette").
Patient reports occasional alcohol use ("I might have a beer during the weekdays...maybe once or twice a month...I'll go out with my friends and we'll drink a lot").
The transcript contains no vital signs or physical examination findings; these are not discussed at any point.

Doctor concludes diagnosis of gastroenteritis based on symptoms ("your symptoms are suggestive of something called gastroenteritis. A bit of a basic infection of your tummy"), which are watery diarrhea, crampy pain, nausea, and systemic symptoms described earlier.

Doctor notes significant fluid loss and concern for dehydration ("You're losing a lot of fluid there" and "if you are getting dehydrated, then we need to do further investigations"), and patient has frequent diarrhea, feels hot, and reduced urine frequency, supporting risk of dehydration.
Doctor recommends oral rehydration solution ("you can get things like diurelite, which is a fluid replacement we can get from the pharmacy. It's probably worth recommending that").
Doctor advises clear fluids and soft diet, advancing as tolerated ("clear fluids you can use soft diet, things like soup, mash, and then gradually build up as much as your body can tolerate").
Patient mentions avoiding milk, but the doctor does not explicitly advise avoiding milk; no dietary restriction on milk is given by the clinician in the transcript.
Doctor tells patient to avoid alcohol ("Try and avoid alcohol if you can").

Doctor instructs to call back if not settling in 48 hours or signs of dehydration ("if your symptoms aren't settling down in the next couple of days, so 48 hours, I want you to give me a call back because...if you are getting dehydrated, then we need to do further investigations").
